import unittest

from depres import max_satisfying, satisfies


class ContractTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Examples taken directly from docs/RANGES.md."""

    def assertSat(self, version, range_, expected):
        self.assertIs(satisfies(version, range_), expected, f"{version} in {range_!r}")

    def test_partial_with_operators(self):
        self.assertSat("2.0.0", ">1", True)
        self.assertSat("1.9.9", ">1", False)
        self.assertSat("1.3.0", ">1.2", True)
        self.assertSat("1.2.9", ">1.2", False)
        self.assertSat("1.2.0", ">=1.2", True)
        self.assertSat("1.1.9", ">=1.2", False)
        self.assertSat("1.1.9", "<1.2", True)
        self.assertSat("1.2.0", "<1.2", False)
        self.assertSat("1.9.0", "<=1", True)
        self.assertSat("2.0.0", "<=1", False)
        self.assertSat("1.3.0", "<=1.2", False)
        self.assertSat("1.2.7", "=1.2", True)
        self.assertSat("1.3.0", "=1.2", False)

    def test_x_ranges(self):
        self.assertSat("1.5.0", "1.x", True)
        self.assertSat("1.5.0", "1", True)
        self.assertSat("2.0.0", "1.x", False)
        self.assertSat("1.2.9", "1.2.x", True)
        self.assertSat("1.2.9", "1.2", True)
        self.assertSat("1.3.0", "1.2", False)
        self.assertSat("0.0.1", "*", True)
        self.assertSat("9.9.9", "", True)
        self.assertSat("1.0.0", "X", True)

    def test_v_prefix_and_build_metadata(self):
        self.assertSat("v1.2.5", "^1.2.3", True)
        self.assertSat("1.2.5+build.9", "^1.2.3", True)
        self.assertSat("1.2.3", ">= 1.2.3", True)

    def test_hyphen_examples(self):
        self.assertSat("2.3.9", "1.2.3 - 2.3", True)
        self.assertSat("2.4.0", "1.2.3 - 2.3", False)
        self.assertSat("2.9.9", "1.2.3 - 2", True)
        self.assertSat("3.0.0", "1.2.3 - 2", False)
        self.assertSat("1.2.2", "1.2.3 - 2", False)

    def test_tilde_examples(self):
        self.assertSat("1.2.9", "~1.2.3", True)
        self.assertSat("1.3.0", "~1.2.3", False)
        self.assertSat("1.2.0", "~1.2", True)
        self.assertSat("1.3.0", "~1.2", False)
        self.assertSat("1.99.0", "~1", True)
        self.assertSat("2.0.0", "~1", False)
        self.assertSat("1.2.3-beta.3", "~1.2.3-beta.2", True)
        self.assertSat("1.2.4", "~1.2.3-beta.2", True)
        self.assertSat("1.3.0", "~1.2.3-beta.2", False)

    def test_caret_examples(self):
        self.assertSat("1.9.0", "^1.2.3", True)
        self.assertSat("2.0.0", "^1.2.3", False)
        self.assertSat("0.2.9", "^0.2.3", True)
        self.assertSat("0.3.0", "^0.2.3", False)
        self.assertSat("0.0.3", "^0.0.3", True)
        self.assertSat("0.0.4", "^0.0.3", False)
        self.assertSat("1.9.0", "^1.2", True)
        self.assertSat("0.2.9", "^0.2", True)
        self.assertSat("0.3.0", "^0.2", False)
        self.assertSat("0.0.9", "^0.0", True)
        self.assertSat("0.1.0", "^0.0.x", False)
        self.assertSat("1.9.9", "^1", True)
        self.assertSat("2.0.0", "^1.x", False)
        self.assertSat("0.9.9", "^0", True)
        self.assertSat("1.0.0", "^0.x", False)

    def test_prerelease_rule_applies_to_every_set(self):
        self.assertSat("1.2.3-alpha", "*", False)
        self.assertSat("1.2.3-alpha", "", False)
        self.assertSat("1.2.3-alpha", "1.x || *", False)
        self.assertSat("1.5.0-beta", "^1.0.0", False)
        self.assertSat("2.0.0-rc.1", "^1.0.0", False)
        self.assertSat("1.2.3-alpha.7", "^1.2.3-alpha.1", True)
        self.assertSat("1.2.4-alpha.1", ">=1.2.3-alpha.1 <1.3.0", False)

    def test_union_with_empty_set(self):
        self.assertSat("5.0.0", "1.x || ", True)
        self.assertSat("1.2.3-alpha", "1.x || ", False)

    def test_invalid_ranges(self):
        for bad in ["1.x.3", ">", "~", "^", "1.2.3.4", "<>1", "1.2.3 - ", "1.2.3-", "- 1"]:
            with self.subTest(range=bad), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                satisfies("1.0.0", bad)

    def test_invalid_version(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            satisfies("1.2", "^1.0.0")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            max_satisfying(["1.0.0", "bogus"], "*")

    def test_max_satisfying_returns_item_as_given(self):
        self.assertEqual(max_satisfying(["v1.5.0", "1.4.0"], "^1"), "v1.5.0")
        self.assertIsNone(max_satisfying([], "*"))
        self.assertEqual(max_satisfying(["1.0.0-beta", "0.9.0"], "*"), "0.9.0")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Summary: range matching (`satisfies`, `max_satisfying`)

## What changed

- `depres/ranges.py`: implemented `satisfies(version, range_)` and `max_satisfying(versions, range_)` per `docs/RANGES.md`.
  - Ranges are parsed into comparator sets joined by `||`. Each comparator is expanded into primitive `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `=` bounds (X-ranges, partials, `~`, `^`, hyphen ranges).
  - Prerelease rule: a prerelease version matches a set only if some comparator in that same set names the same `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with a prerelease tag. Applies to every set, including `*` and the empty set.
  - Both functions accept strings or `Version` objects. Invalid ranges and versions raise `ValueError`. Non-string arguments raise `TypeError`.
  - `max_satisfying` returns the matching item exactly as given, or `None`. It validates every item, including ones that are not the maximum.
- `tests/test_ranges_contract.py` (new file): 13 tests covering the examples in `docs/RANGES.md` and the invalid-input cases. No existing test was edited or deleted.

No files outside `depres/`, `tests/`, and `SUMMARY.md` were changed.

## What I verified

- `python -m unittest` (run from the project root), Python 3.14.3:
  - Before the change: `Ran 8 tests ... FAILED (errors=8)`.
  - After the change: `Ran 19 tests in 0.002s`, `OK`. That is the 8 original tests in `tests/test_ranges.py` plus the 11 new test methods in `tests/test_ranges_contract.py`.

## Not verified / unsure

- I did not run any linter or type checker.
- I did not test edge cases the docs do not spell out. These include `>*` (I made it match nothing), `~*` and `^*` (any release), `~>` (not supported), and unusual whitespace such as `> =1.2`. I chose behavior for these that matches npm where I know it, but I did not compare against npm.
- Build metadata on equal versions: `max_satisfying` keeps the first of two equal versions, so `1.0.0+a` and `1.0.0` tie and the earlier one in the input wins.
- `satisfies` and `max_satisfying` parse the range on every call. There is no cache. That is fine for CI, but the resolver may want to parse once and reuse it.
